title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + background defrag + host-spill paging improvements (v31)
author: Lina Chen
description:
Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and reactive spillover to host memory have been causing elevated tail latency and occasional OOMs under bursty workloads. This PR implements a set of coordinated improvements to eviction heuristics, background defragmentation, and host-spill paging to reduce fragmentation, lower spill frequency, and improve tail latency under realistic request mixes.

Summary of changes: Implemented a weighted eviction priority that accounts for last-access time, access frequency, and fragment size to avoid evicting many small fragments that together cost more to reconstruct. Added an adaptive background defragmentation daemon (kv::DefragCoordinator) that runs at controlled bandwidth and cooperates with the scheduler to avoid impacting latency SLOs. Introduced a compressor-backed host-spill paging layer with page-level reference accounting and async IO to minimize blocking on spill reads. Provided runtime knobs for target fragmentation ratio, defrag throughput cap, spill compression level, and eviction aggressiveness. Added detailed metrics and tracing for fragment histograms, spill/page counters, defrag rate, and eviction decisions.

Why this approach: Prior experiments showed that purely LRU-based eviction disproportionately removes many small KV entries, increasing reconstruction cost and exacerbating tail latency. Combining size-awareness and frequency improves unit-cost decisions. Background defrag reduces long-term fragmentation without blocking hot-path allocations; the adaptive throttle keeps the defrager from interfering with token-serving threads. Paging with lightweight compression reduces resident memory pressure while keeping reconstruction latency acceptable for cold entries.

Compatibility: Feature is behind runtime config flags (kv.enable_adaptive_eviction, kv.enable_defrag_daemon, kv.enable_compressed_spill). Default behavior preserves current LRU for backwards compatibility. Migration notes: operators may enable features progressively (start with adaptive_eviction -> observe metrics -> enable defrag -> enable compressed spill).

Testing & Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks and canary runs on perf-canary showed ~18% reduction in 99.9th percentile latency for a mixed-chat workload (long-context + many small concurrent sessions) and 60% fewer OOM events over a 24h stress window. Unit and integration tests cover eviction ordering, defrag correctness, spill/page reclamation, and CI fuzzed fragmentation scenarios.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation (core algorithms + schedulers)
- [x] Unit tests + integration tests
- [x] Benchmarks on perf-canary
- [x] Docs (runtime flags + ops guidance)
- [x] Metrics + tracing hooks

Related: ENG-9821 (kv fragmentation), ENG-10012 (host spill improvements).
commits: feat(kv): add adaptive eviction strategy (size + freq + recency weighting)
feat(kv/defrag): implement DefragCoordinator with bandwidth throttle and cooperative scheduling
feat(kv/spill): compressed host-spill pages with async IO and page ref-counting
perf(kv): scheduler integrations to deprioritize defrag during SLO pressure
test(kv): unit + integration tests for eviction/defrag/paging
docs: add operator guide and runtime flags for kv cache memory management
diff_snippets: eviction_policy.cpp: introduce ScoreCalculator::score(fragment) combining recency, freq, size; replace simple lru evict list with min-heap by score
defrag_coordinator.cpp: background loop that selects adjacent small fragments and merges them; respects bandwidth_budget and defrag_backoff when SLOs are breached
spill_manager.cpp: page metadata now includes compressed_size and async read path that returns a future; reclaim path decrements page ref-counts
scheduler/throttle.cpp: hooks to detect high-percentile token latency and signal defrag to back off
review_comments: Evan O'Neill: Can you clarify how score weights are derived? We should avoid hardcoding — suggest exposing weights as dynamic config and include a calibration script.
Author (Lina): Added kv.eviction_weights config and included a simple calibration tool (scripts/kv/calibrate_eviction.py) that computes weights from access traces.
Priya Rao: Concern about defrag IO interfering with GPU DMA. How do we ensure we don't cause stalls?
Author: Defrag runs on dedicated threads with cgroup IO limits, uses async IO; added scheduler hint API to reduce defrag throughput when host IO latency rises.
ci_checks: Static analysis/lint: pass (minor style warnings fixed in follow-up commit)
merge_details: Merged via squash on 2024-11-21 by maintainers after approvals from reviewers. No conflicts. Changelog entry added to release notes.
release_notes: Runtime: kv cache adaptive eviction + defrag daemon + compressed host-spill paging. Improves 99.9p latency and reduces OOMs under fragmentation-heavy workloads. Operator flags available for staged rollout.
notes_for_ops: Enable features progressively: set kv.enable_adaptive_eviction=true first, monitor kv.fragmentation_ratio and kv.eviction_spill_count; then enable kv.enable_defrag_daemon with kv.defrag_bandwidth_mbps cap; finally enable kv.enable_compressed_spill. Default flags are false. Refer to docs/ops/kv-cache.md for step-by-step guidance.
benchmarks_summary: Canary results: mixed-chat workload on n1-highmem: 99.9p latency -18%, OOM events -60%, average memory residency reduced by ~12% due to compressed spill and compaction. Defrag cost amortized under 1% CPU on background cores when bandwidth capped.
tests_added: Unit: eviction ordering, score computation, page ref accounting. Integration: defrag merges, spill reclaim correctness, scheduler backoff under SLO pressure. Added perf-canary benchmark config.
